most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Sexually acquired herpes simplex virus (HSV) hepatitis with HSV urethritis, a fulminant or near-fulminant hepatitis. Acute hepatitis A is the main alternative.
one_line_reason: A febrile, sexually active PrEP user with urethral discharge and extreme transaminases in which AST is higher than ALT (8520 vs 5814), a normal WBC, lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly fits HSV hepatitis best. That diagnosis is not in the list. HAV (outbreaks among people with many sexual contacts) is the best listed fit. TDF/FTC PrEP makes acute HBV less likely, and there is no rash or arthritis to suggest disseminated gonococcal infection.
